narrative.overview: Glassbook looks like a well-kept field notebook for glass. Warm paper stock carries navy ink, and a single orange accent stands in for the iris of an aperture. Serif names, sans explains, mono measures. Crisp and tactile: small corners, hairline borders, soft ambient shadows that lift on touch. It is not a generic SaaS dashboard and not a marketplace.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper neutrals with navy ink; one orange accent; teal as quiet secondary.
Serif display, sans body, mono metadata.
Ambient shadows that lift on hover; blurred glass top bar.
Light and dark themes both first-class.

rules.name: The One Aperture Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only accent and marks the one thing to act on or notice on a screen. Teal never competes with it.

rules.name: The Paper and Ink Rule
rules.body: Never pure black or pure white as surfaces or text; neutrals stay warm and tinted toward the paper, with ink tinted toward navy.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif names things, sans explains things, mono measures things. Do not swap roles.

rules.name: The Lift On Touch Rule
rules.body: Raised elements rest quietly and rise only when hovered or focused.

dos: Do use Aperture Orange for the single primary action or notice on a screen.
Do set lens names and headings in the serif, labels in the sans and measurements in mono.
Do keep corners to 2-4px and borders to hairlines; use shadow for response, not decoration.
Do keep both light and dark themes equally finished.
Do use only system fonts and local assets.
Do keep primary controls at least 44px tall and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't make it a generic SaaS dashboard.
Don't use pure black or pure white as a background or text color.
Don't add a second accent color that competes with the orange.
Don't add thick colored side or top stripes to cards for emphasis.
Don't load web fonts, CDNs or other external assets.
